qt: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Hermann Tertsch (PfE) Subject:

A scientific study recently published in the journal Nature indicates that Morocco and Mauritania have received around 75 % of the EU’s financial contributions relating to fishing agreements since 1979 – a total amount estimated to be EUR 3.5 billion. Such contributions, channelled through Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreements, are said to have aided the growth of non-EU fleets that are in direct competition with the fleets of Member States such as Spain and Portugal. In accordance with the agreements signed with Mauritania1 and Morocco2, the financial contributions have been paid to the fisheries ministries of the respective countries, which are the bodies responsible for their management and implementation. In view of the above: 1.

What monitoring, oversight and checking arrangements has the Commission implemented to ensure contributions have been used for their intended purposes, in particular as regards sustainability of resources and development of the local fisheries sectors?
Does the Commission have information on the final recipients of said aid?

Has the Commission assessed the impact of those financial contributions on the competitiveness and viability of fishing fleets in Member States such as Spain and Portugal? What main conclusions has it come to?

(11 March 2026) Pursuant to Article 32(1)(a) of the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation (CFP (1)), a part of the Union’s financial contribution under Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreements (SFPAs) is intended to support the cost of access to fisheries resources in third-country waters. This part of the contribution is not earmarked for specific policy objectives and its use falls under the sovereign discretion of the partner country. In addition, as per Article 32(1)(b) of the CFP Regulation, financial assistance is provided to partner countries aiming at the development of a sustainable fisheries policy driven by the third country (the so-called ‘sectoral support’). As such financial assistance is conditional upon the achievement of specific results, programming and implementation of activities funded by sectoral support are subject to strict monitoring by the Joint Committee of SFPAs, through the regular monitoring by the Commission both in headquarters and in EU delegations. Furthermore, SFPAs define requirements for the administrations of partner countries to ensure transparency, accountability and control of these funds, including a mandatory annual report. Further details and examples can be found in the evaluation and analysis of the SFPAs between the EU and third countries published in 2023 (2) which includes an in-depth analysis of the sectoral support component of the SFPAs, including beneficiaries, as well as in the evaluations conducted before the expiry of each protocol (3). 1 2 ⸱1 ∙
